hints: A number divisible by any selected prime can be counted with inclusion-exclusion.
For every nonempty subset of the given primes, compute their product and add or subtract floor(n/product) according to subset size parity.
Avoid multiplication overflow by stopping when product exceeds n.
analogy: Count multiples of each prime, subtract overlaps, add back triple overlaps, and continue alternating.
example: For n=20 and primes 2,3, count 10+6-3=13 numbers divisible by at least one.
algorithm: Enumerate all 2^k-1 prime subsets. Compute subset product safely; add floor(n/product) for odd subset size and subtract for even, using a wide integer.
correctness: Inclusion-exclusion counts numbers divisible by exactly one or more selected primes with net coefficient one, and nonmultiples with coefficient zero.
complexity: O(2^k) time and O(1) extra space.
